title: Work as an offering
hookLine: Arjuna pushes back on his teacher twice, and gets two great teachings: karma yoga, and God coming age after age.
carry: karma yoga: work as an offering, not for the prize

lines: I TAUGHT THIS TO THE SUN
WAIT: YOU WERE BORN AFTER HIM
cards: Families have a way of keeping each other honest. Tell a story about yourself at a holiday dinner, and someone who grew up with you will say: that's not how it happened.
Something like that happens in the middle of the Gita. Krishna mentions, almost in passing, that he taught this same teaching long ago, to the sun. And Arjuna, his cousin, stops him.
Wait. Your birth came later. The sun was born long before you.
How could you have taught him? Session four of six: the argument in the chariot.

teach.h: WHY PUSH ME INTO THIS ACTION?
teach.b: Read in place, Arjuna is not a polite student. At the start of the third chapter he says, more or less: if understanding is better than action, why push me into this terrible action? You're confusing me.
Tell me one thing for certain. Krishna doesn't send him off to a cave.

teach.h: NO ONE CAN STAY FREE OF ACTION
teach.b: No one can stay free of action, he says, even for a moment. So act, but don't act for the prize. Act as an offering.
He points to King Janaka, who reached the goal through action. Then a line that cuts close: better your own duty, done imperfectly, than someone else's done well.

teach.h: KARMA YOGA: WORK AS AN OFFERING
teach.b: Hindus call this teaching karma yoga, the path of action. Your work, done fully and offered to God, becomes worship, and the result is left in God's hands.
Krishna had already said it in the chapter before: your right is to the work, never to its fruits. That doesn't mean don't try. It means don't let the prize own you.
Then the fourth chapter, and the moment from the hook. When Arjuna objects that Krishna was born after the sun, Krishna says: many births have passed for both of us. I know them all, and you don't.
Whenever dharma fails, I come, age after age, to protect the good and set dharma right. The cousin in the driver's seat is beginning to show who he is. And it happens because Arjuna argued.

how: The Gita's third chapter is traditionally titled Karma Yoga, the yoga of action, and many Hindus close a task or a puja with 'Krishnarpanam astu', let this be offered to Krishna.

the fourth chapter of the Gita, where Krishna speaks of his births

s: Krishna told Arjuna to give up action and retreat to think
he said no one can stay free of action; act, but as an offering, not for the prize.
karma yoga means not caring how hard you work
it means working fully and offering the result to God, without clinging to it.
Krishna said it is better to do your own duty imperfectly than another's well
that's his line in chapter three: better your own duty, even done imperfectly.

games.q: you're Arjuna. you've asked: if understanding is better than action, why push me into this? what does Krishna answer?
o: give up action and go think in the forest.
no one can stop acting, so act as an offering, not for the prize.
fight to win, whatever it takes.
games.why: no one stays free of action even for a moment, Krishna says. act, and offer it: that's karma yoga.

practice: Many Hindus close a task or a prayer with the words Krishnarpanam astu: let this be offered to Krishna. Let your hands rest open and think of one ordinary task waiting for you. Breathing in, see yourself doing it fully.
Breathing out, offer how it turns out: the praise, the grade, whether anyone notices. If you pray, you can say those words, or your own. If you don't, simply let the result go.

wordCard.voice: Bhishma Parva. The book where a soldier argues with his teacher in the middle of a battlefield, and the argument opens the door.
